security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences and inline backticks being misread as executable backtick syntax. Confirmed concerns are the dual-use APK reverse engineering purpose, a specific nmap network scanning recommendation, and guidance that connects credential extraction with IoT device testing. The skill includes authorization and responsible disclosure language, but marketplace users should receive clear scope warnings.

remediation.issue: Network scanning guidance appears in the IoT integration section.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the nmap recommendation or require an explicit authorized-scope check before any network scanning workflow.

remediation.issue: Credential extraction guidance is paired with testing against IoT devices.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite the workflow to focus on documenting hardcoded credentials and prohibit reuse outside an approved test plan.

remediation.issue: Command examples use placeholder paths and broad grep patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to quote user-provided paths, avoid destructive locations, and review output before sharing findings.

content.user_title: Decompile Android APKs for Security Review
content.value_statement: Android APK reviews often need readable source, resource context, and systematic security searches. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through jadx-based decompilation and focused analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to decompile APK files with jadx CLI and jadx-gui.
Shows when to enable deobfuscation, fallback mode, and resource-only analysis.
Guides searches for credentials, endpoints, crypto use, storage patterns, and WebView issues.
Outlines workflows for security assessment, IoT app analysis, batch processing, and endpoint discovery.
Describes how to combine jadx output with apktool and runtime analysis.
Provides troubleshooting steps for obfuscation, memory limits, slow decompilation, and GUI issues.
limitations: Requires jadx and a Java runtime to be installed before use.
Decompiled Java is approximate and may not match original source code exactly.
Heavily obfuscated or protected apps may produce incomplete or incorrect output.
Users must have permission to analyze the APK and verify findings through runtime testing.

use_cases.title: Mobile App Security Review
use_cases.description: Decompile an authorized APK and inspect source code for common Android security weaknesses.

use_cases.title: IoT Companion App Assessment
use_cases.description: Map endpoints, authentication flows, and device communication patterns in an IoT app.

use_cases.title: Application Behavior Analysis
use_cases.description: Understand app logic, entry points, resources, and network clients from a released APK.

prompt_templates.title: Decompile One APK
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me decompile this APK with jadx, choose an output directory, and explain the resulting source and resource folders.

prompt_templates.title: Search for Security Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through authorized searches for hardcoded credentials, endpoints, storage issues, crypto use, and WebView risks in the decompiled output.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Obfuscated App
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a jadx workflow for an obfuscated APK, including deobfuscation, fallback options, and how to triage unreadable code.

prompt_templates.title: Build an IoT App Review Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized IoT companion app assessment using jadx output to identify API endpoints, authentication flows, and device discovery behavior.

output_examples.input: Review an authorized APK for hardcoded credentials and network endpoints.
output: A decompilation plan that separates source review from resource review.
A prioritized checklist for credentials, URLs, authentication code, and certificate pinning.
A short findings format that records file paths, evidence, impact, and verification status.

output_examples.input: The APK is obfuscated and jadx output is difficult to read.
output: A workflow using deobfuscation, fallback mode, and targeted class searches.
Guidance on reading partial code safely without assuming it matches original source.
Recommendations for cross-checking static observations with runtime behavior.

output_examples.input: Assess an IoT companion app with permission from the device owner.
output: A source review path for API definitions, base URLs, authentication headers, and discovery logic.
A list of evidence to collect before testing any device communication.
A reminder to keep testing scoped to authorized devices and networks.

best_practices: Confirm written permission and scope before decompiling any APK.
Use deobfuscation for production apps and preserve original outputs for comparison.
Verify static findings with runtime behavior before reporting security impact.
anti_patterns: Do not decompile apps that you do not own or have permission to assess.
Do not treat decompiled Java as exact original source code.
Do not reuse discovered credentials or test devices outside the authorized scope.

faq.question: Does this skill install jadx?
faq.answer: No. It assumes jadx and Java are already installed and guides their authorized use.

faq.question: Can it recover original source code exactly?
faq.answer: No. Jadx produces approximate Java from bytecode, so names and control flow may differ.

faq.question: Is jadx-gui covered?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains when to use the GUI for interactive browsing, search, and cross-references.

faq.question: Can it help find hardcoded secrets?
faq.answer: Yes, for authorized APKs. It provides search workflows for credentials, tokens, URLs, and related patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace dynamic testing?
faq.answer: No. It recommends validating static findings with runtime analysis where possible.

faq.question: What are the main safety requirements?
faq.answer: Use it only with permission, respect licensing, and keep testing within the approved scope.
